newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman to enlist banks' help in funding big projects.
newsitem.headline: Oman to enlist banks' help in funding big projects.

text.p: Oman has said it would enlist the help of commercial banks in financing big private sector projects, but the state would extend soft loans to smaller projects that require up to 250,000 rials capital investment.
A decree by Sultan Qaboos, published in the latest official gazette, said the state would contract commercial banks to lend money to projects costing between 250,000 and five million rials.

Beneficiaries would pay only the prevailing standard rate applicable to state soft loans, while the government would pay the difference to the commercial banks, which would have to tender for the business.

For small loans up to 250,000 rials extended by the state's Omani Development Bank, the government would pay six percent of the nine percent interest charged by ODB. Beneficiaries would pay three percent.
Oman, like other Gulf Arab states, is trying to diversify its economy away from reliance on oil and to give the private sector a leading role.
The decree said projects qualifying for state-supported loans would have to be 51 percent owned by Omanis. They should be in agriculture, industry, export, tourism or education.
Loans would be extended only to firms with at least 40 percent of their capital open to the public, it said.
